route.geometry: optional 6 s detour used in LP2: 50-50 the sculpture in the pit right of spawn (goal at 1:52)

route.to: top of the curving concrete road
route.geometry: ≈ 30-40 m curving road with parapets climbing ≈ 3 m; BS 50-50 on its edge for a $50 at 1:19; Brooklyn Bridge comes into view
two rebar bars jut from the broken slab and droop toward the plaza; BS tailslide the right bar (1:15-1:14)
Re-Rebar (50) at 1:13 with a $50 on the hop; the left bar's start is hidden until you are nearly on it (halfglassgaming) and it curves inward (thumbsticks)
FS tailslide; tape on screen ahead at 1:12
grind ollie off the end; tape collected in the air at 1:11; land on the plaza by the benches at 1:10 (or on the rail below: Rebar to Rail Gap)

skillGates: knowing the Banks exist and how to enter (low wall, fallen pole, or subway after 5 tokens)
early blind hop to a second bar whose start is hidden
collectibles.coupling: subway route needs all 5 tokens; taxi traffic on the start street; trains on the El; token-free entries exist (low brick wall per RPGC; fallen pole per absolutcheats/thumbsticks)
collectibles.failure: a missed hop drops ≈ 3 m to the Banks plaza; re-climbing the road takes ≈ 8-10 s (LP2 climb 0:29:58-0:30:05). Leaving the Banks (≈ 11 s via low wall/kicker) and returning by subway costs ≈ 30-40 s of a 120 s run
collectibles.timeFromSpawnS: ≈ 49 (LP2 run 2, spawn 1:59 at 0:29:20, tape 1:11 at 0:30:09, including the Joey's and subway-rails goals); escalator top -> tape ≈ 32; Banks landing -> tape ≈ 13
collectibles.why: The tape is the payoff for finding the hidden district; the earned access route (tokens -> subway) chains goals and lands at the foot of the tape road; once inside, the local test is a short, cheap-to-retry blind rail-to-rail hop
collectibles.evidence: VG; LP2 0:29:20-0:30:12 and 0:30:33-0:30:44; PS12 ny-city; WEB rpgclassics; WEB absolutcheats; WEB thumbsticks; WEB halfglassgaming

guidance: S visible from spawn above the park wall; the opening wall line collects it
Letters and tokens sit on park features visible from the park paths
The El overhead from spawn is a standing landmark to the station and the Banks
The goal list itself (tokens open the subway; Grind the Subway Rails) points to the El, which ends in the Banks
The Banks are walled off and lower; the tape is not seen until the rebar line (LP2 0:30:08); the second bar's start is hidden
A road that stops in mid-air with rebar pointing outward signposts the tape line
BIG DROP sign at the river fence; taxi and trains are the hazards
designLogic: The tape lives in the level's hidden district; entering it is the main challenge and the local line is short (13 s from the landing)
Several entries with different prices: free but knowledge-gated (low wall, fallen pole) or earned (5 tokens -> subway)
Goal chaining: tokens -> subway -> subway-rails goal en route -> lands at the foot of the tape road; LP2 clears three goals in a 49 s opening
Construction motif marks the tape line: an unfinished road with rebar says 'go to the end'
The skill test is one blind, early rail-to-rail hop (knowledge + timing, not speed or height)
The tape sits inside a scoring line (Rebar to Rail Gap, Bench-Hoppin'); 4 of 5 Banks cash icons are on the approach
Failure is cheap locally (≈ 8-10 s re-climb) and expensive globally (≈ 30-40 s to leave and return)
The pocket has its own exits (blue kicker, low wall), so it never traps the player
All five letters are in the park near spawn and complete within 30 s; the easiest goal is nearest
Tokens use the park's furniture and pay off with mobility, not just cash
Hydrants drag the player around the outer streets against traffic
Goal cash rises with distance: tape $1200 > subway rails $1100 > Joey's $900 > tokens/SKATE $800 > hydrants $700
Moving hazards (taxi, trains) add timing to both access routes
remakeChanges: Tape unchanged: rebar right -> rebar left -> jump off (PS12; thumbsticks; halfglassgaming)
Banks access: remake guides route via the subway after the 5 subway cards; thumbsticks grinds up a pipe leaning on a fence (both versions keep several entries)
Tokens renamed Subway Cards; subway stays unlocked permanently (PS12)
Added pickups: 4 stat points (one on the tape's rebar line), VV logo on an awning off the El tracks, alien plushie behind a QP
Gap list: 41 on VG -> 43 in PS12 (adds One Side, Downhill Jam)
transfer: Broken-road rebar crystal: a ≈ 3 m climbing curved ramp ending in mid-air with two short drooping rails; rail B starts hidden behind the parapet; crystal ≈ 1-1.5 m above and ≈ 1 m beyond B's end so only the grind ollie (≈ 2.4 m pop) reaches it; 2.1 m snap radius keeps the blind hop forgiving

Earned fast route + free hard route: tokens or a trick gate open a long descending elevated rail to the crystal ramp; keep a token-free entry (30° fallen pole grind or a wall within the ≈ 4.6 m on-foot double jump)
Moving hazard on the access rail: a travelling rail or moving-platform train on the descent
Pocket with exits: a kicker or speed pad that throws the rider back over the wall to the main street
Silhouette as signpost: an unfinished structure whose open end points at the crystal; crystal hidden until the final rail
Scoring line beyond the crystal: a landing rail or bench row under it
openQuestions: Exact tape height (no side view; 3-4.5 m is from the rider camera in LP2)
Whether RPGC's low-brick-wall entry and absolutcheats' fallen-pole entry are the same feature
One cash icon ($100) may be missing from VG given RPGC's '$500 + $1000' (Philadelphia's figure matches its icon total)
Original (PS1) gap point values; only remake values are listed
RPGC places the E 'on the far corner from where you started', unlike VG/LP2
